_comment: Tier-2 for fourc::constraint#2, and a correction of the key name. Mortar coupling does need its interface integration configured, but there is no INTPOINTS_MORTAR in 4C — writing it is a parse error, 'Could not match this input'. The key is NUMGP_PER_DIM in the MORTAR COUPLING section and it is only consulted when INTTYPE is Elements or Elements_BS. On upstream meshtying3D_elebased: omitting it leaves the default 0, refused with 'Invalid Gauss point number NUMGP_PER_DIM for element-based integration.' from contact/src/4C_contact_meshtying_strategy_factory.cpp; a value of 1 is refused by the same message from a different guard; 7 runs and still meets the deck's 1e-08 result test. The arm worth remembering is INTTYPE Segments with the same NUMGP_PER_DIM still present: the number is not ignored, it is reinterpreted as a triangle rule and the run dies deeper in with 'unknown tri gauss rule' from mortar/src/4C_mortar_integrator.cpp. PARSER_SUGGESTS_THE_RIGHT_KEY=0 records that the parser offers no hint toward the correct spelling. Verified by execution 2026-08-06 against 4C 2026.2.0-dev (git 89519cf).
expect_in_output: Invalid Gauss point number NUMGP_PER_DIM for element-based integration.

_mutation.note: remove the pathology from the omission arm: keep NUMGP_PER_DIM. That arm then runs to completion and the Gauss-point refusal disappears, so the fixture must go red.
remove the pathology from the INTTYPE arm: leave INTTYPE at Elements, where the shipped NUMGP_PER_DIM is valid. The triangle-rule failure then never happens and the fixture must go red.
remove the pathology from the key-name arm: spell the key the way 4C spells it. That arm then parses and runs, so 'Could not match this input' disappears and the fixture must go red.
